stem: Two independent samples are drawn from a factory's production records. Sample A has a minimum value of 12 units and a coefficient of range of 0.50. Sample B has a minimum value of 28 units and a range of 18 units. When the two samples are combined into a single data set, what is the range of the combined data?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student adds the two individual ranges: range_A (= 24) + range_B (= 18) = 42. This is incorrect because ranges are not additive when combining groups.
Student computes only the range of Sample A (= max_A - min_A = 36 - 12 = 24) and ignores Sample B entirely.

From Sample A: (max_A - 12)/(max_A + 12) = 0.50, so 0.5*max_A = 18, max_A = 36, range_A = 24. From Sample B: max_B = 28 + 18 = 46. Combined: overall min = min(12, 28) = 12, overall max = max(36, 46) = 46. Combined range = 46 - 12 = 34.
Student computes max_A - min_B = 36 - 28 = 8, incorrectly pairing the maximum of one sample with the minimum of the other.

explanation: Step 1: Back-calculate max_A from the coefficient of range. (max_A - 12)/(max_A + 12) = 0.50 gives 0.5*max_A = 18, so max_A = 36 and range_A = 24. Step 2: max_B = min_B + range_B = 28 + 18 = 46. Step 3: Combined range = overall max - overall min = max(36, 46) - min(12, 28) = 46 - 12 = 34.

explanation_sections.punchline: Combined range needs the global maximum and global minimum; derive each group's extremes independently, then compare all four.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the two-step setup: (1) recover max_A from the coefficient equation, (2) recover max_B from range. Then combined range = max(max_A, max_B) - min(min_A, min_B) = 46 - 12 = 34. Do NOT add individual ranges.
explanation_sections.lesson: The range of a combined data set is NOT the sum of individual ranges; it is determined solely by the global extremes.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 seconds. Solve for max_A (45 sec), then derive max_B (15 sec), then compare all extremes (15 sec). The classic trap is adding the two ranges (24 + 18 = 42).
